data.name: RS1001_Title
data.value: Thread.Sleep detected inside async method

data.name: RS1001_MessageFormat
data.value: Hold on! Thread.Sleep() is blocking a real thread inside an async method. Under load, this starves the thread pool. Swap it for 'await Task.Delay()' — your app will thank you.

data.name: RS1001_Description
data.value: Thread.Sleep blocks the calling thread completely, preventing it from doing any other work. Inside an async method, this defeats the purpose of async/await and can cause thread pool starvation under high load. Replace it with 'await Task.Delay()' to keep your app healthy and scalable.

data.name: RS1002_Title
data.value: Task.WhenAll fan-out may be unbounded

data.name: RS1002_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! Task.WhenAll is processing a Select() projection without an explicit limit. Under heavy input, this can flood dependencies. Consider bounding concurrency (for example: Take(...), chunking, or SemaphoreSlim).

data.name: RS1002_Description
data.value: Task.WhenAll over an unbounded Select projection can trigger too many concurrent operations at once, causing connection pressure, timeouts, or cascading failures. Add an explicit concurrency boundary before fan-out.

data.name: RS1003_Title
data.value: Parallel.ForEach may run without an explicit concurrency limit

data.name: RS1003_MessageFormat
data.value: Careful! Parallel.ForEach is running without ParallelOptions/MaxDegreeOfParallelism. On shared resources, this can create saturation spikes. Consider defining an explicit limit.

data.name: RS1003_Description
data.value: Using Parallel.ForEach without an explicit MaxDegreeOfParallelism may oversubscribe CPU, connection pools, or downstream services. Set a bounded degree to keep load predictable.

data.name: RS1004_Title
data.value: Blocking async flow with Task.Wait/Result

data.name: RS1004_MessageFormat
data.value: Yikes! Blocking on Task via .Wait() or .Result can starve threads and increase deadlock risk. Prefer 'await' to keep async flow healthy.

data.name: RS1004_Description
data.value: Calling Task.Wait() or reading Task.Result blocks the current thread. In async-heavy code paths, this can reduce throughput and increase deadlock/starvation risk. Use await-based flow instead.

data.name: RS1005_Title
data.value: Potentially heavy ToList() materialization

data.name: RS1005_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! This LINQ pipeline is being materialized with ToList() without an explicit Take(...) limit. On large datasets, this can increase memory pressure.

data.name: RS1005_Description
data.value: Materializing a LINQ pipeline with ToList() too early or without bounds can allocate large collections and increase GC pressure. Consider adding a limit or streaming strategy when possible.

data.name: RS1006_Title
data.value: HttpClient instantiated inside method scope

data.name: RS1006_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! Creating HttpClient inside a method can lead to socket exhaustion and slower communication under load. Prefer IHttpClientFactory or a reused instance.

data.name: RS1006_Description
data.value: Instantiating HttpClient per operation may create excessive socket churn and connection pressure. Reusing HttpClient or using IHttpClientFactory improves connection reuse and communication stability.

data.name: RS1007_Title
data.value: HTTP call without explicit timeout policy

data.name: RS1007_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! This HttpClient call has no explicit timeout (Timeout property or CancellationToken). Under latency spikes, requests may hang longer than expected.

data.name: RS1007_Description
data.value: HTTP communication should define explicit timeout boundaries to avoid stuck calls and cascading latency. Configure HttpClient.Timeout or pass a CancellationToken with timeout control.

data.name: RS1008_Title
data.value: Retry loop without explicit max attempts

data.name: RS1008_MessageFormat
data.value: Careful! This retry loop appears unbounded (infinite condition without explicit exit). Under persistent failure, it may amplify load and latency.

data.name: RS1008_Description
data.value: Unbounded retries can create feedback loops against unstable dependencies. Define an explicit maximum number of attempts and fail fast with observability.

data.name: RS1009_Title
data.value: Retry policy without exponential backoff

data.name: RS1009_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! Retry in HTTP path appears to use fixed delay. Without exponential backoff, repeated failures can amplify pressure on unstable dependencies.

data.name: RS1009_Description
data.value: Using fixed delay in retries can keep hammering a failing dependency at high frequency. Prefer exponential backoff (ideally with jitter) to smooth retry traffic.

data.name: RS1010_Title
data.value: Retry policy without jitter

data.name: RS1010_MessageFormat
data.value: Heads up! Retry appears exponential but without jitter. Multiple clients may retry in lockstep and create traffic spikes.

data.name: RS1010_Description
data.value: Exponential backoff without jitter can synchronize retries across instances, causing burst pressure on unstable services. Add random jitter to spread retry attempts.

data.name: RS1011_Title
data.value: async void method outside event handler

data.name: RS1011_MessageFormat
data.value: Method '{0}' is declared as async void. Exceptions thrown here cannot be caught by the caller and will crash the process. Use async Task instead.

data.name: RS1011_Description
data.value: async void methods are only safe for event handlers. In any other context, exceptions escape the call stack and propagate to the SynchronizationContext, usually terminating the application. Return async Task or async Task<T> instead so callers can await and handle exceptions properly.

data.name: RS1012_Title
data.value: String concatenation with += inside a loop

data.name: RS1012_MessageFormat
data.value: String concatenation with '+=' inside a loop allocates a new string on every iteration. Use StringBuilder to avoid excessive GC pressure.

data.name: RS1012_Description
data.value: Strings are immutable in .NET. Using '+=' inside a loop creates a new string allocation on every iteration, which increases memory pressure and can trigger frequent GC collections under load. Replace with StringBuilder and call ToString() once after the loop.
